## What's changed

* Download original photos saves every photo as a JPEG (#105). TikTok lists each photo as a HEIF copy first, so they were landing as .heif files that a lot of gallery apps and computers can't open, and some phones, Samsungs included, can't decode TikTok's HEIF at all. Hushfeed now takes the WebP copy TikTok lists beside each HEIF and saves it again as a full-size JPEG on Android 9 and newer. When TikTok lists a JPEG copy, that one is saved byte for byte instead. A photo that can't be converted keeps the file TikTok sent, and so does one with see-through parts. The setting's description says JPEG now too, and story photos work the same way.
* Hiding the status bar now also removes the black strip TikTok keeps above videos for it, and on Android 14 and older the video draws behind the camera cutout instead of below it (#97). A new Hide the Clear display controls switch takes the close button, progress bar and pause and speed buttons off the screen while Clear display is on, along with the close button photo posts show in the corner. They're back the moment you leave Clear display.
* Clear Display now hides the stories button above Following when TikTok leaves it up, and puts it back as soon as you leave Clear Display (#84). Pause leaves both the stories button and the top tabs to TikTok. Automatic Clear Display also waits until TikTok has really cleared the screen before it counts a try, so a first video TikTok wasn't ready for still gets cleared.
* Automatic Clear Display retries on the current video after focus returns, including the first video after startup (#84). A canceled or failed attempt no longer prevents another try. Manual exit remains respected, and callbacks from an earlier video cannot cancel the next video's timer.
* Back up, Restore and Import watch history don't get stuck behind a slow file app anymore. If the file app hasn't answered after a few seconds, the row offers to stop waiting, and stopping before anything was read or written leaves your settings and history as they were. A backup the file app already has is the one exception: the row says the file app hasn't said yet whether it saved it, and you get the real answer once it does. A file app that never lets go of a file holds only that row, which says so, instead of piling more work up behind it. Turning the phone mid-restore keeps the restore going.
* Feature Gate Lab's Export loaded values and Import loaded values don't get stuck behind a slow file app anymore. If the file app hasn't answered after a few seconds, the Lab offers to stop waiting, and stopping before anything was read or written changes nothing, not even a file you picked to replace. Tapping either one again while a file is still out says so, where it used to queue another to run whenever the first one ended. Exporting over an older, bigger export no longer leaves the end of the old file behind, which made the new one unreadable.
* Picking an existing backup file to replace no longer risks losing it. If the backup stops, or fails before anything goes into the file (a feed rule list too long for a backup, say), the file you picked keeps your older backup instead of being deleted. An empty file the picker made for the backup is still cleaned up.
* Settings search lists the rows where your search is a whole word first. Searching "counts" used to put Hide verified accounts and Blocked creators, where it only turns up inside "accounts", above the rows that are about counts. Rows that match only inside a longer word still follow, in page order, and translated settings sort by the same rule.
* Settings search now finds every box in a checklist, ticked or not, so searching "counts" finds Counts under the buttons in the right column list. Opening a box's result opens the list scrolled to that box without changing it. A list that's open when the screen rotates comes back with your unsaved ticks.
* Switch rows in Hushfeed's settings change shape when the screen is narrow and the text is large. The switch moves under the text, at the end of the row, and the title and description get the whole width. A German title at twice the text size on a small phone no longer breaks mid-word into four short lines. Wider screens keep the usual layout, and a row scrolled from one shape into the other changes back.
* What's new now tells you the notes are in English when the rest of the settings are in your language. The notes are also marked as English text for screen readers.
* Undo clearing seen videos now restores history in the background and reports how many cleared records still fit the history limits. It no longer says videos were restored when newer watches leave no room for them. A failed save keeps Undo available.
* Undo now commits watches recorded during restoration before counting them. Older queued writes also preserve newer watch times that Undo has already saved.
* Media saves now honor the server's full retry delay, including HTTP dates, before following a redirect or trying another mirror or subtitle track. A delay beyond the save's time limit stops the job with a clear message and keeps files already saved. Cancel also interrupts a retry wait.
* Saving a diagnostic report or a feature gate report runs on a thread of its own, so a slow media store can't hold up the threads the rest of Hushfeed shares. Tapping Save again while a report is still saving says so instead of starting a second one.
* Hushfeed now builds on Morphe patcher 1.15.1, so it needs Morphe Manager 1.34.0 or newer. Manager 1.33.0 asks for an update before it loads the bundle. ARSCLib follows the patcher to 9b742c412d, with its hashes checked against the downloaded files, and the release checks patch with desktop CLI 1.18.1.
* Every Guava request in the build now resolves to 33.7.2, the release outside GHSA-xxph-c9ww-hj94, across the settings, plugin and project graphs rather than only where the catalog's pin reached. Its checksums were verified against Maven Central before the strict dependency check accepted them. Guava stays on the build and patching side: the patch bundle and the extension carry none of it. The check that patch sources don't import Guava directly used to pass without reading a file. It reads them now.
* An edit to the Java extension alone no longer reruns the fingerprint checks against the APK fixtures, since those never read it. Full test commands and release checks still cover every test, and a change to a patch, a test, a dependency or a fixture still reruns them.
* Documentation edits no longer rerun unchanged APK fixture tests. Full test commands and release checks still cover every test, and source-reading checks now track their external inputs. Replacing an APK invalidates test results even when its size and timestamp match.
* Local storage scanner checks now keep Java diagnostics visible without treating successful runs as failures in Windows PowerShell.
* Local APK signing now accepts harmless Java startup diagnostics from heap and CPU limits. Invalid certificates and failed signing checks still stop installation.

**From the tracker**

This release moves HushMessenger to Messenger 582.0.0.61.92 and adds seven switches, Auto reply and Use your own font among them.

### Reported issues

- [#29](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/29) Messenger 582.0.0.61.92 is supported now, all 14 arm64 builds of it. 580 and 581 are dropped.
- [#42](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/42) **Auto reply** is new. It answers messages with replies you write, by the words you pick or any message at all.
- [#41](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/41) With **Hide read receipts** on, opening a chat doesn't send Seen any more, and the chat stays unread in your list. Mark as read and Mark as unread work again.
- [#20](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/20) **Hide read receipts** now points to Messenger's own **Read receipts** setting, for when you'd rather have opened chats marked read on your phone without the other person seeing Seen.
- [#40](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/40) **Use the phone's camera app** opens your camera app from a chat's camera button again.
- [#39](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/39) **Use your own font** is new under Theme. Pick your phone's font or a .ttf or .otf file.
- [#36](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/36) **Turn off the swipe up for disappearing messages** is new under Conversations.
- [#37](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/37) With **Stop analytics uploads** on, an upload it skips lets the phone go back to sleep right away instead of holding it awake for up to 90 seconds.
- [#30](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/30) With **Hide People You May Know** on, your chats show up sooner after Messenger starts.
- [#38](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/38) **Fix shared videos with xHE-AAC sound** is new. It converts that sound to regular AAC when you share such a video into Messenger, so it can be sent.

### New

- HushMessenger now patches Messenger 582.0.0.61.92, all 14 arm64 builds APKMirror lists for it, and no longer accepts 580.0.0.49.91 or 581.0.0.49.91. Morphe Desktop applies every patch to each of the 14 builds. Messenger 582 looks up some of the names HushMessenger uses to tell its built-in switches apart instead of spelling them out, so the two business suggestion switches now follow that lookup. Meta also reworked the code behind the Settings row in the menu, the avatar tab in the sticker keyboard, the inbox tabs, kept unsent messages, **Save any story** and **Send videos without re-encoding**, and each of those patches now finds its spot in both ways 582 builds lay it out.
- **Auto reply** is a new Conversations switch, off until you turn it on ([#42](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/42)). Tap **Edit replies** under it to write up to 20 replies, each with the words that should trigger it, split by commas. A message that has one of those words, matched as a whole word in any case, gets that reply. Leave the words empty and the reply answers any message. The reply goes out through the Reply button on Messenger's own notification, so it works in encrypted chats too, and each chat gets at most one auto reply every five minutes. Group chats are left alone unless you tick **Answer in group chats too**.
- There's a new **Use your own font** switch under Theme, off to begin with ([#39](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/39)). With it on, Messenger's own text uses your phone's font instead of Meta's Optimistic font. Below the switch in HushMessenger settings you can also pick a .ttf or .otf file of up to 20 MB, and Messenger's text uses that font instead. The row shows just the file's name and whether it's in use. Emoji stay as they are. A change shows after Messenger restarts.
- Conversations gets **Turn off the swipe up for disappearing messages**, which starts off ([#36](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/36)). With it on, swiping up at the bottom of a chat no longer turns on disappearing messages, so a scroll can't set the timer by accident. Scrolling works as usual, and you can still turn disappearing messages on from the chat's settings. It takes effect right away, with no restart.
- **Fix shared videos with xHE-AAC sound** is a new Conversations switch, off until you turn it on. Messenger can't send a video whose only sound is xHE-AAC, which Facebook and Instagram now use for some videos, so sharing a saved one into Messenger ended in "Unable to send". With the switch on, Messenger's copy of a video you share into it gets that sound converted to regular AAC before anything reads it. The picture is copied as it is, and videos with any other sound aren't touched.
- **Stop ad attribution uploads** joins the Privacy switches, off until you turn it on. With it on, Messenger's ad attribution job stops before it reads your phone's advertising ID, whether through Google's library or its direct Play services fallback, so the request that sends Meta the ID and your ad tracking setting never gets built. The saved attribution state stays as it was, and turning the switch off lets the next run go ahead as before. The ID itself doesn't change.
- **Stop inbox and ad link logging** is another new Privacy switch, and it starts off. With it on, Messenger skips two reports. One says which part of your chat list was on screen, each time the visible chats change, and Messenger files it under its inbox ads. The other says which ad and business page brought you in when a link from an ad opens a chat in Messenger. Only the reports are skipped. The code around them, which keeps track of what's on screen, still runs, and turning the switch off lets the next report through.
- **Hide ad banners in business chats** is new too, under Conversations and off by default. When you start a chat with a business by tapping one of its ads, Messenger shows that ad in a banner at the top of the chat. **Hide chat promotions** never covered it, because it isn't a promotion banner, so it gets its own switch. With it on, the banner isn't added the next time you open such a chat.
- HushMessenger settings has a **Support HushMessenger** row at the end of the App tab. It opens my Ko-fi page in your browser, if you'd like to buy me a coffee.

### Changed and fixed

- With **Hide read receipts** on, opening a chat no longer marks it read or sends Seen, and it stays unread in your chat list ([#41](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/41)). Mark as read and Mark as unread in the chat list work again, and so does Mark as read on a notification. Those show Seen, like Messenger does. Replying in a chat marks it read too, since your reply shows you saw it anyway.
- **Hide read receipts** now points to Messenger's own **Read receipts** setting under Settings > Privacy & safety. With that turned off and **Hide read receipts** left off, a chat you open is marked read on your phone and the other person doesn't see Seen ([#20](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/20)).
- **Use the phone's camera app** now works from a chat's camera button on Messenger 582. That button starts Messenger's camera a different way there, so the switch never saw the tap and Messenger's own camera kept opening. Now your phone's camera app opens, and the photo you take opens in Messenger's editor for that chat. Messenger checks where a picked photo comes from before it opens one, and it refused this photo because the screen that hands it over runs inside Messenger. It lets that one photo through now, and every other file still gets Messenger's usual check ([#40](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/40)).
- With **Stop analytics uploads** on, a skipped upload now tells Messenger right away that the phone can go back to sleep. Before, each upload Messenger started directly could keep the phone awake for up to 90 seconds ([#37](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/37)).
- With **Hide People You May Know** on, HushMessenger asks Messenger for your chat list again about half a second after it starts instead of after 2.5 seconds, to shorten the loading circle that could still sit under your chats for a few seconds. It tries up to three more times in the first 8 seconds and stops as soon as your chats show up ([#30](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/30)).
- **Stop analytics uploads** now also skips the timer that sends Messenger's native analytics batch every three minutes. It leaves crash reports alone.
- **Copy setup** now lists each folder in Messenger's data whose name mentions analytics, with how many files it holds and how big it is, so you can see whether Messenger's analytics pile up while **Stop analytics uploads** is on. It shows names and sizes, never what's in the files.
- Restoring saved choices on Android 9 or 10 now reads the right part of the file when the app you pick it from hands it over as a stream that starts partway in.
- The checks that find the code each patch changes now accept only what Messenger 582 ships. The extra shapes they used to allow for 580 and 581 are refused now, so a build that brings one back stops with an error before anything is changed.
- **Stop analytics uploads** now also covers the way Google Play can hand Messenger's Google Play upload service a task directly, without starting it the usual way. With the switch on, that task is reported back as done right away, so Google Play doesn't retry it, and Messenger's other scheduled tasks on the same worker run as before.
- **Keep a message log** now deletes messages older than 30 days from the saved file itself, a little after Messenger starts and every six hours, instead of only hiding them until the next message arrives. That happens with the switch off too. Off stops saving new messages and keeps the old ones until they expire or you clear the log, and the log's screen now says so. Each message keeps up to 8,000 characters and the whole log stays under 2 MB, dropping the oldest first. If the saved file can't be opened any more (say the phone's key store lost its key), it's moved aside and the log starts fresh instead of failing on every message. A save that fails partway leaves the old log as it was, and **Clear log** also drops messages that arrived a moment before but weren't saved yet, so they can't show up again afterward.
- **Restore old emoji drawer** and the Meta AI tab part of **Hide Meta AI** keep the answer Messenger got when it started, so a change waits for a restart. Their rows in HushMessenger settings now say so ("Takes effect after Messenger restarts", or "Stays in effect until Messenger restarts" after you turn the switch off or pause), and Copy setup marks them with `until_restart`. An account Meta never moved to the redesigned emoji drawer has nothing to wait for, so its row doesn't say that.
- Tapping a row in Messenger's menu after scrolling it now opens that row. Messenger reuses rows as the menu scrolls, and one that had been showing the HushMessenger entry could open HushMessenger settings instead of its own screen.
- With **Material You theme** on, a color that one of Messenger's theme methods just takes from another is now changed once instead of twice.
- **Spoof package version** now refuses a number lower than the Messenger you're patching. The Play Store would keep offering that same release as an update, and the patched app couldn't install over the version it came from.
- **Keep a message log** holds on to messages when a save fails and tries them again first, in the order they arrived. A message dated in the future gets corrected in the saved file too, not only on screen. If you repatch without the switch, the saved log and its key are deleted the next time Messenger starts. On Android 13 and newer the log's screen stays out of the Recents preview.
- **Send photos at original quality** now cleans its copies older than a week out of Messenger's cache. Up to 20 MB each could pile up there before.
- TalkBack can now reach the message log's **View log** and **Clear log** buttons. Buttons that can't be used right now look grayed out.
- The message log now says who sent each message, and in a group which chat it came from ("Ana in Weekend trip"), taken from Messenger's own notification for that chat. Before, entries were grouped under a long chat code. Messages saved before this update show as "Unknown chat".
- When someone unsends a message, the message log keeps the original and no longer gains a second line like "Ana sent a message." for the unsend. That stand-in doesn't get an auto reply either.
- The message log saves each message once. Messenger can build one message's notification twice, and both copies used to land in the log. A message that **Auto reply** answered also says who sent it now, instead of "Unknown chat".
- Restoring choices from a file that can't be read now says "Couldn't read that file" instead of calling it an invalid backup. Canceling a restore partway says your choices didn't change.
- Several lines in HushMessenger settings read more clearly, like the restart hint, the empty search result, the export and import help, and error lines, which now point to **Copy setup** for details. A switch used more than two days ago shows days ("Used 3d ago"). **Chat heads** is written the same way everywhere.
- **Hide Meta AI** now also covers the list that opens when you type @ in a chat. Meta AI and imagine drop out of it, while the people in the chat still show. In a community chat the community's AI entry goes as well. Turning the switch off brings them back on the next letter you type.
- With **Hide Meta AI** on, the search bar above your chats drops its "Ask Meta AI or search" hint and shows Messenger's plain one.
- **Restore screens on re-signed builds** now also answers the certificate check in Messenger's own push service, which reads the signature by itself instead of asking the method the patch already covered. That service matters most on phones without Google Play services.
- **Use system emoji** tries adding Messenger's emoji font behind the phone's up to three times when it fails, since a font that's still being written can fail once.
- HushMessenger publishes its app shortcuts in the background now, so they don't hold up Messenger's startup on a Root Mount install.
- On a Root Mount install, **Copy setup** now says how long HushMessenger took to start when Messenger first needed it, and on which thread. That shows whether it's slowing Messenger's startup down.
- More of the checks that find the code each patch changes now refuse a spot the patch's code couldn't work in, like a register its call can't reach, a field Messenger's code isn't allowed to read, or a static method where it needs an instance, before anything is changed. The patch descriptions also say that the Meta AI tab goes after a restart.
- The release and install check scripts now report a damaged profile record or a signer line without a key with a clear error instead of crashing. Nothing changes in the patches.
- On an install that has no screen for opening your phone's camera app, like a Root Mount install, **Use the phone's camera app** is grayed out and says why. Before, it looked on while the chat camera stayed Messenger's own.
- Releases now run from `scripts/release/release.ps1` in five stages that refuse to run out of order. Each Messenger build family gets patched once per release, and the release checks can wait for a free build slot instead of piling onto other builds. Nothing changes in the patches.
- Extended the app audit with actual Messenger packet observations, background job and CPU measurements, and physically unplugged battery readings. Revision 2 includes aggregate data, a charge-counter chart and a repeatable procedure. It distinguishes shared encrypted hosts from specific tracking operations and documents the limits of short observations on a paused installation. No patch behavior changed.
- Added a detailed Messenger internals audit with ad and tracking paths, native settings screenshots, the boundaries of the 37 controls at v0.22.0, and patch candidates with acceptance criteria. A reusable 581 DEX query batch accompanies the report. The audit identifies a conditional analytics Binder entry outside the existing guards and documents message-log isolation and retention limits. No patch behavior changed.
- The README now points to the patch code, in-app settings, build profiles and catalog checks. It also walks through adding a control or a supported Messenger version.
- **Material You theme** is now in Morphe Manager's default selection, so every control is there without Expert mode. Its switch is under Theme on the Controls page and starts off, so a build patched with the defaults looks like Messenger until you turn it on. **Clone install under another package name**, **Spoof package version** and **Custom new-message sound** still need Expert mode, because they change the package or need a file you pick.
- Every patch description in Morphe Manager now says in plain words what the patch changes and why you might want it. It ends with where to turn it on, or says it works as soon as you patch it in.
- Every switch in HushMessenger settings now explains in plain words what it does and what you'll notice. The pages, the setup panel and the bubble and app icon help text got the same plain wording.
- Messages in HushMessenger settings are clearer. Saving and restoring your choices, update checks, the camera notice and the setup help now say what happened and what to do next.
- The options you fill in when patching are easier to read. Clone install, Custom new-message sound and Spoof package version now explain what to type, and the version code option is called Version number.
- The settings extension's unit tests now always run on JDK 21. On Windows, the Java 25.0.2 runtime bundled with Android Studio made four Android 9 and 10 restore tests read the start of a file instead of the part the provider pointed to. Restoring choices on a phone was never affected.

This release has 43 patches, 37 of them switches, for all 37 arm64 builds of Messenger 580.0.0.49.91 and 581.0.0.49.91. It fixes the loading circle under the chat list ([#30](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/30)), the Like with Use system emoji ([#34](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/34)) and the story ring after an anonymous view ([#35](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/35)). Eight new switches start off, and three new patches that change the package itself start unselected, including Custom new-message sound ([#32](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/32)).

- `Keep emoji search on emoji` is a new switch under Stickers that starts off. With it on, typing while the emoji keyboard is open no longer flips it over to sticker search, so you stay on emoji. It takes effect right away, with no restart.
- `Use the phone's camera app` is a new switch under Conversations that starts off. With it on, the camera button in a chat opens your phone's own camera app instead of Messenger's camera. The photo comes back into Messenger's photo editor for that chat, the same way a photo picked from another app does, and you send it from there. It's photos only. HushMessenger has the camera app save the photo to Messenger's cache, not your gallery. Checks cover the chat camera button in all 37 supported builds.
- `Pure black dark mode` is a new switch under Appearance in settings, shown when Material You theme is patched in, and it starts off. With both on, Messenger's darkest dark mode backgrounds turn pure black. Lighter surfaces keep their wallpaper tint, and light mode doesn't change. You can flip it without patching again.
- `Send videos without re-encoding` is a new switch under Conversations that starts off. Messenger already skips the re-encode for a video that's close to its target size. With the switch on, a video up to 25 MB takes that same passthrough instead of being re-encoded. Bigger videos still get Messenger's compression, and so do trimmed or edited ones and formats Messenger won't pass through. Checks cover the video transcoder in all 37 supported builds.
- `Clone install under another package name` is a new patch, unselected by default. It installs a second Messenger beside the first under its own package name and app name, `com.facebook.orca.hush` and `Messenger Clone` unless you choose others in Morphe. Messenger's own permissions, provider authorities, task affinities and push categories move to the new name, and the patch stops before changing anything if one of them would still clash. The encrypted chat backup lookup that crashes under a renamed package keeps working, with a fix adapted from rushiranpise's Change package name patch. The broadcasts Messenger sends to itself, like the ones that refresh message requests and inbox filters, reach the clone's own package instead of the original app. Links it opens inside itself, from a notification or a story for example, stay in the clone too. HushMessenger's settings, launcher shortcuts and `Restore screens on re-signed builds` follow the new name. The README covers what stays tied to Messenger's original name.
- `Copy setup` now shows whether Android knows HushMessenger's settings provider under the package name Messenger runs as.
- `Unlock app icons` is a new switch under Theme that starts off ([#33](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/33)). With it on, every icon in Messenger's App icon setting can be picked without a subscription, and Messenger changes the home screen icon with its own code, the same way it applies a free icon. The icons already ship inside the Messenger APK, so nothing gets downloaded. Messenger still decides whether the App icon setting shows on an account, and with the switch off it may put its default icon back the next time it closes. Checks cover the icon code in all 37 supported builds.
- With `Hide People You May Know` on, the chat list no longer keeps a loading circle under your chats after Messenger restarts ([#30](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/30)).
- With `View stories anonymously` on, a story you've opened no longer keeps its new-story ring in your chat list, after a restart too ([#35](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/35)).
- With `Use system emoji` on, a Like in the chat list shows Messenger's thumbs-up again instead of an empty box ([#34](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/34)). The phone's emoji font doesn't have Messenger's own Like character, so on Android 10 and newer that character now comes from Messenger's emoji font while every other emoji keeps the phone's look. It also shows on the first start after an update, when Messenger draws the chat list before its own emoji font has loaded.
- `Spoof package version` is a new patch that starts unselected. It sets Messenger's version code to a number you choose, 2147483647 by default, so the Play Store stops offering Meta's updates over a patched build. Messenger may report that number to Meta. Later builds need the same number or higher to install over it. The patch catalog now lists each patch's options.
- `Custom new-message sound` is a new patch that starts unselected ([#32](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/32)). Pick an .ogg, .mp3, .m4a or .wav file of 1 MB or less when you patch, and it replaces Messenger's `new_message` sound, the one its message notifications use by default. With no file picked it changes nothing. A missing, empty, oversized or mislabeled file stops the patch with the reason.
- `Restore old emoji drawer` is a new switch that starts off. It turns off Meta's redesigned emoji drawer, so the emoji keyboard keeps its earlier layout. Changes apply after `Restart Messenger`, and accounts Meta never moved to the redesign see no difference.
- `Stop analytics uploads` is a new switch that starts off. It stops the background services Messenger's analytics logger uploads through. Messenger still records those events on your phone, and they can upload after you turn it off.
- `Keep a message log` is a new switch that starts off. It copies each message as its notification arrives, so an unsend can't take it back, and it's the only switch that reaches end-to-end encrypted chats. The log holds only messages that raised a notification. It stays on your phone and is encrypted with a key kept in the Android keystore, so the copy never leaves the device. A new viewer in settings lists it newest first, and `Clear log` deletes the file and throws the key away. Nothing is stored while the switch is off or Pause or safe mode is on.

Refresh the HushMessenger source in Morphe and patch again. Compare the bundle with `SHA256SUMS.txt`, which is signed with the release key (`SHA256SUMS.txt.sig`).

This release has 33 patches, 30 of them switches, for all 37 arm64 builds of Messenger 580.0.0.49.91 and 581.0.0.49.91. It adds Messenger 581 and a new switch, Hide joined community chats. Hide AI sticker tools now covers the Generate buttons in the sticker keyboard, and Allow screenshots covers view-once media and Quicksnap.

### New

- HushMessenger now patches Messenger **581.0.0.49.91** as well as 580.0.0.49.91 ([#29](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/issues/29)). All 16 arm64 builds APKMirror lists for 581 pass the compatibility checks, and Morphe Desktop 1.18.1 applied all 33 patches to each of them with a 1 GB heap. On a Galaxy S22, v0.14.0 on Messenger 580 updated in place to this release on 581 and kept its sign-in and chats. Meta renumbered two server flags and moved several screens around in 581, so People You May Know, joined community chats, inbox ads, the AI sticker Generate buttons, screenshots in view-once media, Native Bubbles and the HushMessenger menu row now follow the new layout. On 581 the HushMessenger row sits right under Settings, above the new QR code row. The 580 builds patch exactly as before.
- Hide joined community chats is a new control that starts off. It filters subscribed channels and announcements from the main Chats list (the All chip) while keeping conversation data, delivery and unread state intact. Displayed row counts follow the filtered list. Off or Pause restores the original list on the next render. Other chips such as Channels and Unread, search and community folders keep their rows. Folder and membership checks cover all 21 supported builds.
- **Hide AI sticker tools** also hides the Generate buttons in Messenger's newer sticker keyboard. The guard matches the verified AI label and leaves other cells alone. **Allow screenshots** also covers the secure-window calls in view-once media and Quicksnap. It preserves unrelated flags, lifecycle code and the original calls while off or paused. All 21 supported builds have records for these routes.
- Settings expose each control's full row as one accessible switch. The title, description and activity label share a touch target, and the switch keeps its keyboard focus. Unavailable controls can be read but can't be toggled. Live TalkBack checks on an isolated Android 16 preview read the title and description as one control and changed the saved choice once per double-tap. The enabled-count summary stays readable without announcing after every toggle. Regression checks cover Android 9 and 16.

### Changed and fixed

- Patch builds now use Morphe Patcher 1.15.1 and the maintained MorpheApp ARSCLib fork. The tested tools are Morphe Manager 1.34.0 and Morphe Desktop 1.18.1. Migration checks applied all 32 patches to all 21 supported APKs at a 1024 MB heap, verified signatures for the five naming groups and retained their native libraries. Two fresh checkouts produced the same bundle bytes. Kotlin and Bouncy Castle security pins remain in place.
- The install check reads signer details from Android Build Tools 37 as well as 36.1. Build Tools 37 labels each signer with its signature scheme, and the check used to stop with "Cannot establish the complete current signer set" when it saw that format.
- The early v0.0.2 to v0.0.8 previews are no longer marked as pre-releases on GitHub. Catalogs that follow pre-releases kept offering v0.0.8 from them, and that stops on their next refresh.
- Inbox switches such as Hide People You May Know, friend requests and growth prompts now give one steady answer to each chat list Messenger builds. Messenger asks the same question when it lists a section, when it starts the section's loading and when it stops it, and a switch flipped in between now waits for the next chat list instead of splitting those steps. **Restart Messenger** applies a change everywhere at once.
- The full compatibility check now requires the exact stock APKs. Community fixtures use recorded stock identities, and media replay goes through shared discovery. Tests track fixture changes and reject duplicate builds that would leave another build untested.
- File tests now share Android's atomic-replace semantics on Windows, check post-commit read failures, and cover nonseekable restores on Android 16. Community discovery also reuses its constructor identifier in both scans.
- Retained unsent markers are capped at 4,096 IDs and no longer share the settings monitor. This only prunes markers, never message content.
- Choices saves check media-row ownership before opening the destination for writing. A picker can't use a Messenger-owned MediaStore row to overwrite its content.
- An original-photo success callback that throws no longer receives a second failure callback or loses the copy it was handed.
- Theme return hooks keep incoming branches attached to the color helper. Menu binding rejects reused holder registers before making changes, and the story Save helper is retained even when the patcher has already cached direct methods.
- Community filtering preserves the native list type and checks backward and switch branches before reusing temporary values. Screenshot support now stays unavailable if any matching viewer method changes, even when the original methods still exist. Other controls remain available.
- Profile recording now parses the rebuilt manifest, resource table and every DEX. A successful Desktop report and valid ZIP are no longer enough to accept malformed APK contents.
- Changed media-viewer or community code now leaves those controls unavailable while other patches can still apply. Community discovery runs once during setup and reuses fixed method identifiers while checking the APK. Manager 1.33.0 applied all 33 patches to Messenger 581 at its unchanged 640 MB limit, with a 288 MB peak.
- Closing settings or canceling an update check no longer waits for a slow cache write. Pending writes from canceled checks are discarded, and an older write cannot replace a newer result.
- Saving choices continues through rotation or closing settings, with the same 30-second limit and a completion or failure message. Closing the screen no longer cancels a save after its destination may have been emptied. Restores still cancel when settings close.
- Compatibility profiles now require Desktop to apply every patch and rebuild the APK before the record is written. Discovery alone could previously accept a changed menu or drawer that the patcher rejected. The check rejects incomplete results and changing input files.
- **Open** in settings and **Restart Messenger** now find Messenger when you've switched to one of its alternate app icons. They used to report that no launcher was available, because they read each icon's built-in default instead of whether Messenger had turned it on.
- Safe mode keeps counting startup crashes even when its saved count can't be read, so a crash loop still pauses the controls after three tries.
- Update checks recover on their own if GitHub's reply no longer matches the saved release details. A retry time from GitHub never holds checks back for more than a day, and it never shortens the normal wait between failed checks.
- Development release checks compare the held public feed with the one published under its release tag, and the development version must be newer. Catalog validation runs the Gradle wrapper directly and stops the whole process tree if it times out. The compatibility report keeps going when the community route changes on a new build, and the memory gate reports a damaged output APK without dropping the other results.
- The memory gate now checks every build of every supported Messenger version. It used to expect exactly 21 and would have refused to start once 581 was added.
- The memory gate runs at most two builds at once, with two processors per Java process. Compatibility and patching failures include their subprocess exit codes. Regression tests check that all inputs run without exceeding the concurrency limit.
- Focused dependency tests run five partial patch selections through compilation. A failed sibling keeps the successful patch, advertises no failed control and leaves its own native target unchanged. A later selection starts with no stale keys. Each run checks a single settings and extension injection.
- Opted-in update checks reuse validated release details for an hour and send their ETag on later checks. GitHub retry times are shown in settings and respected. Quota reset times apply only to an exhausted quota, so secondary limits keep their own retry wait. Release links must match their tags, and development builds ahead of the public release show both versions. Late replies can't save cache data after cancellation.
- Copy setup includes the control descriptions shown in settings and explains what recorded activity proves. Receipt wording keeps the local unread and reply limits explicit. Sign-in and past-call-log documentation now reflect the observed results.
- Original-quality photos enforce the 20 MB limit throughout preparation and delivery. Files that grow during a read or while a callback waits are rejected. Cleanup keeps the source and earlier copies intact. Existing scan bytes, color profiles and orientation handling are preserved.
- Crash records verify replacement contents before committing them. Android 9 and 10 check the backup rename before a write can overwrite the old record, and a completed save won't trigger a rollback. Recovery checks preference saves too. If a save fails, settings keep the controls paused and show a retry message. A successful recovery restores the saved theme immediately. Invalid preference types keep host startup disabled. Existing records remain readable.
- Development bundles can be validated while the public feed remains held. Validation checks both DEX files, including mapped section counts, bounds and referenced item starts, and the exact loaded catalog. Cached catalog comparisons preserve JSON types. Validation freezes the bundle with its checksum outside the build folder. The memory gate uses that snapshot and checks that its bytes stay unchanged. Release validation keeps its publication checks separate.
- File saves and restores can be canceled. Settings stop waiting after 30 seconds and release the screen when it closes. Late results can't change choices, and a storage app that ignores cancellation can't start unlimited background work. File slices retain their absolute boundaries, including files supplied with a different initial position. If you cancel a save, save again before you rely on that file.
- Repository links now use the HushMessenger artwork as their social preview.
- Manager 1.33.0 applied all 32 patches at its existing 640 MB process limit, with a peak heap of 290 MB. The signed result passed archive checks and kept every native library unchanged. Fresh-checkout reproduction and non-English setup diagnostics also passed. A development build updated an existing signed-in installation without replacing its key or losing its chat history.

HushMessenger v0.14.0 is for Messenger 580.0.0.49.91 and works on all 21 arm64 builds. It has 32 patches, and 29 of them are switches you turn on in settings.

This is the first release since v0.8.0, so it rolls up a few days of work. The big additions are Native Bubbles and an optional slide when you open a chat.

**New**

- **Slide chats in and out** (#28) slides a chat in from the side when you open it from your chat list or search, and back out when you go back. The screen underneath holds still, and right-to-left languages slide from the left. It starts off. Pause or Android's **Remove animations** setting keeps Messenger's own transitions.
- **Allow chat bubbles** now offers **Stock**, **Chat Heads** and **Native Bubbles** (#19). Native Bubbles uses Android's own bubbles on Android 11 and newer, so a chat can open as a floating bubble. Your account still has to qualify, and Android has to allow Messenger's bubbles. A link to Android's bubble settings sits right below the mode buttons.

**Fixes and changes**

- Settings open from Messenger's side menu now, as well as from its Menu tab (#26).
- **Use system emoji** draws your phone's own emoji on Android 12 and newer (#25). It used to load Google's emoji every time, so Samsung phones and emoji modules lost their own set.
- On a Root Mount install, Android never reads the patched long-press shortcuts, so **Patch controls** and **Restart Messenger** were missing from Messenger's icon. HushMessenger adds them itself now when Messenger starts (#27).
- The directions to settings now say **Long-press Messenger's home screen icon > Patch controls**. "Long-press Messenger" was easy to read as the title inside the app (#27).
- Saving and restoring choices with a file only works with documents you pick, never Messenger's own private files, and it shows progress while it works. A restore that takes a while won't undo switches you changed in the meantime.
- **Original-quality photos** strips the small preview thumbnail some cameras tuck into the photo header. The main image, its color profile and density info stay as they were.
- Settings and the install guide explain that uninstalling the settings icon removes Messenger too. Use **Hide app drawer icon** to hide just the icon.

**Updating**

1. Use Morphe Manager 1.33.0 or newer and refresh the HushMessenger source. It should show v0.14.0 with 32 patches. On a computer, Morphe Desktop needs 1.17.0 or newer.
2. Patch an unmodified arm64 Messenger **580.0.0.49.91**. Any of the 21 version codes listed under Supported Messenger builds in the README works, for example 346013440 or 346013387. The 32-bit builds aren't supported.
3. Sign with the same key you used last time and install over your current copy. A different key means uninstalling Messenger and losing its local data.
4. Open HushMessenger settings and tap **Restart Messenger**.

The `.mpp` file is a patch bundle for Morphe. It isn't an APK you can install.

**Known limitations**

- Opening a chat from a notification with Slide chats in and out turned on hasn't been tried on a phone yet, and neither has Android 13 or older.
- Native Bubbles hasn't been tried on a custom ROM or a low-memory phone.
- The Root Mount shortcut fix was checked on a rooted test emulator, not a rooted phone.
- Hide read receipts can leave your own copy of a chat marked unread (#20).
- Nobody has checked a fresh sign-in or recovering encrypted chat history on a phone yet, and live ad removal is still unconfirmed.

**Validation**

- 147 Kotlin tests, 458 Android unit tests and 47 Python checks pass. Android lint reports no errors.
- Morphe Desktop 1.18.0 applied all 32 patches, Material You included, to every one of the 21 supported builds with a 1024 MB Java heap.
- One build from each of the five groups that share internal names (346013440, 346013372, 346013423, 346013357 and 346013374) was also patched and signed, and apksigner verified every v3 signature.
- On an Android 16 test phone, chats slid in from the chat list and from search in both themes, and turning the switch off brought back Messenger's own transitions.
- Two clean builds of the bundle, one of them from a fresh checkout of the release commit, came out byte for byte the same.
- OSV-Scanner found no known advisories in anything the bundle ships. Its only hits are old Commons Lang and Apache HTTP libraries inside Android's lint tool, which isn't part of the bundle.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt.sig` is signed with the release key `SHA256:Z+UfHy7IUbtgNRO/wHkIr68+u4I+SIKPY9avfx/VAPU`. The README shows how to check it with `ssh-keygen`.

The full list is in the [changelog](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushMessenger/blob/v0.14.0/CHANGELOG.md).

HushMessenger v0.8.0 is for Messenger 580.0.0.49.91 and works on all 21 arm64 builds. It has the same 31 patches as v0.7.0, and 28 of them are switches you turn on in settings.

The fix a lot of you were waiting for is in here. Patching with **Material You theme** selected no longer runs Morphe Manager out of memory (#18). Thanks to everyone who reported it and posted what they saw.

**New patches**

None this time. The App tab does get one new feature:

- **Save choices to a file** and **Restore choices from a file** go through Android's file picker, so HushMessenger doesn't need storage access. The file uses the same format as the clipboard backup. If you cancel, or pick a file that's damaged or isn't a backup, nothing changes.

**Fixes and changes**

- **Material You theme** checks every spot it changes before it edits anything. That keeps a full patch run within a 1 GB heap, the limit people ran into in #18, on every supported build.
- Safe mode has a **Resume** button now. If you'd already turned on **Pause all changes**, the button reads **Clear safe mode** and leaves Pause alone. Your saved choices stay either way.
- Crash recovery reads Android's own record of why Messenger stopped. When Android closes Messenger for low memory or an app update, that no longer counts toward safe mode, and the same crash can't be counted twice.
- **Open** in settings takes you to Messenger instead of back into settings.
- The status line under each switch refreshes when you come back to settings. Paused switches say **Changes paused**, and the text is easier to read in both themes.
- **Keep unsent messages** now explains right beside the switch what it covers (#23). It works on Messenger's older unsend path. End-to-end encrypted chats aren't covered, and group chats haven't been checked. Its activity line only moves when it really catches an unsend, and two unsends arriving together can't overwrite each other anymore.
- When **Hide app drawer icon** isn't offered, the App tab says why, for example on a Root Mount install. Searching settings for "drawer icon" takes you there (#6).
- The update check shows that it's working and has a **Check now** button if it fails. Turning it off or closing settings stops a check that's still running. It only trusts a small, well formed reply that points at this repository.
- Restoring a backup checks the whole thing first, so one bad line means nothing changes instead of half a restore. Older clipboard backups still work. Switches a backup doesn't mention keep their current setting.
- Tapping a backup button twice quickly no longer opens two pickers.
- The Menu tab's HushMessenger row checks every place it edits before it changes any of them.

**Updating**

1. Use Morphe Manager 1.33.0 or newer, since that's the version the memory fix was tried with, and refresh the HushMessenger source. It should show v0.8.0 with 31 patches. On a computer, Morphe Desktop needs 1.17.0 or newer.

3. Sign with the same key you used last time and install over your current copy. A different key means uninstalling Messenger and losing its local data.
4. Open HushMessenger settings and tap **Restart Messenger**.

The `.mpp` file is a patch bundle for Morphe. It isn't an APK you can install.

**Known limitations**

- Saving and restoring choices with a file has only been covered by the automated tests. It hasn't been tried on a phone yet.
- The Android 17 crash records are covered by tests, but no phone running Android 17 has tried this build.
- Morphe Manager was tried at its 1 GB limit with build 346013440 while this was being built. The release bundle itself was checked at that limit with Morphe Desktop on all 21 builds.
- Keep unsent messages doesn't work in end-to-end encrypted chats, and group chats haven't been checked.
- After you view a story anonymously, the ring around that person's picture in your chat list still shows the story as new until it expires.
- Nobody has checked a fresh sign-in or recovering encrypted chat history on a phone yet, and live ad removal is still unconfirmed. Builds 346013354, 346013370, 346013394 and 346013423 patch cleanly but haven't been installed on a phone.

**Validation**

- 121 Kotlin tests, 352 Android unit tests and 47 Python checks pass. Android lint reports no errors.
- Morphe Desktop 1.18.0 applied all 31 patches, Material You included, to every one of the 21 supported builds with a 1024 MB Java heap and without forcing compatibility. Each output had the settings code and the expected number of theme edits, and the stock files were unchanged afterwards.
- One build from each of the five groups that share internal names (346013440, 346013372, 346013423, 346013357 and 346013374) was also patched and signed, and apksigner verified every v3 signature.
- Two clean builds of the bundle, one of them from a fresh checkout of the release commit, came out byte for byte the same.
- OSV-Scanner found no known advisories in anything the bundle ships or the patch build runs. Its only hits are old Netty and Apache HTTP libraries that the Android Gradle plugin keeps for its device test runner, which this build doesn't use.

- [#7](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/7) asked to hide the Instagram button on profiles. The new `Hide the Instagram button` patch takes it off your profile and everyone else's. Its switch is in HushThreads settings under More settings > Appearance, and it starts off.
- [Hushfeed #122](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushFeed/issues/122) asked about the thought bubbles on Threads profile pictures. The new `Hide ghost post bubbles` patch takes them off. Its switch is on the same Appearance page and starts off too.
- [#6](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/6) found thousands of threads in Threads' push process. 0.0.12 fixed the main cause. This release also closes the push process every time Android stops its service, so the next start is a fresh one, and the process closes itself if it ever runs past 600 threads. Both fixes come with every build. I tried it on my phone by coming back to Threads six times, two minutes apart, and each time the push process started fresh and closed again. It's also the most likely cause of the battery drain someone mentioned on Reddit.
- [#5](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/5) asked for a pure black (AMOLED) theme. `Pure black dark mode` works on Threads 450 and is in Manager's default selection now, so you don't need Expert mode for it. Turn it on under More settings > Appearance.
- [#4](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushThreads/issues/4) asked to keep your place when you come back to Threads. `Block background-return feed refresh` is in the default selection now as well (its switch is Keep feed position on return, under Feed), and the release check makes sure all four of its hooks land in Threads 450.

I'll keep each of these open until whoever reported it tells me it's working for them.

## Threads

- This release patches Threads 450.0.0.51.78 only, the newest stable version. 449.0.0.54.82 and 448.0.0.54.85 aren't offered any more, so if you're still on one of them, update Threads to 450 before you patch. From here on each release moves to the newest stable Threads and drops the one before.
- New `Hide the Instagram button` patch takes the Instagram button off the top of profiles, yours and other people's, and leaves the other buttons where they are. Its switch is on the Appearance page under More settings and starts off. Restart Threads after you change it.
- New `Hide ghost post bubbles` patch takes the little thought bubbles off profile pictures, the one on a profile and the row of them at the top of your feed. The pictures and the ghost posts themselves stay, and tapping a picture works as before. Its switch is next to Hide the Instagram button on the Appearance page and starts off. Restart Threads after you change it.
- `Hide suggested users` now keeps the Suggested for you accounts off profiles too, yours and other people's, and leaves the rest of the profile alone. It's the same switch under Feed, still on by default, and Search and Activity keep their suggestions. A profile that's already open keeps what it showed until Threads draws it again.
- `Disable video autoplay` now also holds an Instagram video shown inside a post, trend previews and the videos in ad cards, so they wait for a tap the way feed videos do. It's the same Tap to play videos switch under Feed, and the full-screen viewer still plays and pauses them as before. This passes fixture checks on Threads 450 but hasn't been tried on a device yet.
- The 0.0.12 fix for threads piling up in Threads' push process now comes with every build. It used to ride on `Restore screens on re-signed builds`, so a build made in Expert mode without that patch went without it. Without it, the push process on a re-signed build can stop and restart itself in a loop that piles up thousands of threads in under a minute. It's now part of `HushThreads settings`, which every other patch needs, and has no entry of its own in the patch list.
- Threads' push process still gained about seven threads every time you came back to Threads after more than a minute away. Android stops the push service when Threads has been in the background for about a minute but keeps its process, and each restart left the stopped service's threads running. Now the push process closes once its service has stopped, and the next start gets a fresh one, the same as after Android frees memory. It also keeps count of its own threads while it runs and closes itself past 600 (it normally runs about 60), so a runaway like the thousands in one report can't keep growing. Like the fix above, it comes with every build.
- Morphe Manager's default selection now holds every patch but three, so you don't need Expert mode to get `Disable video autoplay`, `Pure black dark mode`, `Max image quality`, `Disable screenshot detection` or `Block background-return feed refresh`. Those five start with their switches off, and a fresh patch looks like the Threads you know until you turn things on in HushThreads settings. `Change version code` stays out because it changes the version Android sees, so going back to stock Threads means uninstalling. `Remove share targets` and `Trust user-added certificates` stay out because they change Threads when you patch and there's no switch to undo them. Turn on Expert mode to pick those three.
- If you'd picked one of those five patches before and never changed its switch, the switch starts off after you update. HushThreads keeps no record of the build you came from, so it can't tell you meant it on. Look these over in HushThreads settings and turn back on the ones you want. Under Feed that's Keep feed position on return, Tap to play videos and Full size photos. Under Privacy it's Hide screenshots from Threads, and under Appearance, in More settings, it's Pure black dark mode. A switch you'd already turned off stays off.
- `Save photos and videos` moves from Feed to a Downloads group in Expert mode's patch list, the same name its page has in HushThreads settings.
- Every patch description says what the patch does, where its switch is in HushThreads settings and how that switch starts, so Manager's list tells you what you're getting before you patch.
- Patch descriptions in Morphe Manager are rewritten in plain English. Each one says what the patch changes, why you might want it, and ends with where its switch is and whether it starts on or off.
- Setting rows in HushThreads settings are reworded in plain English, with a restart reminder on Pure black dark mode. Translations for German, Spanish, Indonesian, Brazilian Portuguese and Turkish are updated to match.
- A few messages are clearer about what happened and what to do next: a failed download, the cancel hint while saving, an unreadable reply from GitHub, and the status line on the overview. Translations are updated to match.
- The settings home page ends with Support HushThreads, which opens the Ko-fi page in your browser. If nothing on your phone can open it, a tip shows the address and Threads keeps running.

## Docs

- The README's Trust user-added certificates section now says which connections your certificates reach. Android's standard check honors the patched file, but Threads' own network stack still wants one of Meta's built-in keys on the connections it pins, so a debugging proxy can't read that traffic.
- Added a Threads APK reference and app audit covering feed ads, tracking identifiers, analytics patch boundaries, and customization opportunities. Added patch authoring guidance and corrected the install example to use the primary 450 target.
- Added a stock 450 walkthrough with settings screenshots, measured network and background observations, and explicit battery-measurement limits. Confirmed the profile Instagram button and separate profile suggestions, and expanded the patch guide's registration and coverage checks.

## Tooling

- Settings and Turkish translation tests now match the wording shipped in HushThreads.
- The desktop CLI runs, bundle merges and the resource, register, signing and fingerprint checks now wait for a slot of the machine's build queue when `BUILD_QUEUE_SCRIPT` names one, and run straight away when it doesn't. Before, they started beside whatever builds were running and the queue never saw them.
- The device scripts no longer cut a longer device lease down to 20 minutes when they renew it, so a lease taken for a long check can't lapse in the middle of it and hand the device to someone else. They also read a lease's end time in UTC under PowerShell 7. A lease written with a `Z` used to read back as local time, which west of UTC kept an expired lease looking valid for hours.
- The patch tests that read the Threads fixtures run as their own Gradle task, `:patches:fixtureTest`, with each fixture's path and SHA-256 as its inputs. A change to the fixtures reruns only those tests, and a fixture swapped for another of the same size and date still counts as a change. Each build's dex is now read and parsed once per test run rather than on every lookup. `:patches:test` still runs every test, and refuses a run where a fixture test skipped with the fixture folder set.
- The pre-push gate runs Gradle twice. Everything but the fixture tests goes first, so a failing quick test or lint stops the push in minutes, and the full run with the fixture tests comes second. `scripts/release/release.ps1 -Stage preflight` runs the quick checks a release needs in about five minutes: the advisory comparator, the script contracts, that same quick patch run, the translation and release-check tests, both lints and the release facts.
- A release can patch each Threads fixture once instead of twice. `verify-all-patches.ps1 -KeepIn <folder>` keeps a passing run with a stamp naming the bundle, APK, patch list and CLI by SHA-256, and `build-release-receipt.ps1 -AppliedDir` reads a kept run whose stamp still matches and runs every check on it. Any other fixture is patched as before.
- The release check accepts `* **Docs:**` bullets in the section being released, the way it accepts `* **Tooling:**` ones. Morphe Manager shows neither, and neither counts as a Threads change. Before, a release whose section held a Docs bullet was refused.
- A release now runs in five stages from `scripts/release/release.ps1`, one command each, in the order `prepare`, `preflight`, `build`, `publish` and `index`. Prepare makes the version and changelog edits for you to review and commit. Preflight now runs the release text tests too, then pushes the prep commit through the gate. Build patches each fixture once for the receipt and tags the commit only after everything passed. Publish checks every hosted asset against the built one before it changes the repository description, and index writes the index commit and pushes it. A stage won't run before the one it follows, and one that stopped part way can be run again.
- Release preflight clears the test results its filtered extension run leaves behind. Gradle keeps only the classes a run touched, and the push right after read that partial set for the commit it carried and stopped there, so preflight's own push failed every time before the gate ran a test. Build still reruns every test before anything is counted.
- The register check accepts the version code `Change version code` writes. `verify-all-patches.ps1` applies every patch, that one included, and the check refused the build because its version code no longer matched stock. With the patch selected, the patched build now has to carry exactly the raised code, and without it the codes still have to match.
- The final APK check now holds `Block background-return feed refresh` to its own contract, the way it already holds `Hide ads` and five other patches. It finds Threads' four return checks in the stock build by what they log and how they decide, and the patched build has to ask the extension once at each: first thing in the hot-start decision, right before the reset to main feed returns, right before the warm-start check stores its answer, and where For you's swap joins its two answers. Left out, the patch has to leave those four methods as Threads wrote them. Before, a hook that still landed but no longer saw the answer it's there to change would've passed.
- The final APK check now holds `Disable video autoplay` to its own contract too. It finds PostVideo and its playback effect in the stock build by the notes Compose leaves in them and works out which of PostVideo's booleans decides whether its video plays (the fourth on 450). The patched build has to ask the extension about that flag right before every call a single post or a carousel makes to PostVideo, with any branch to the call landing on the question, and PostVideo and the effect have to stay as Threads wrote them, so the full-screen viewer plays as it always has. Left out, nothing may ask and those methods stay stock. Before, a build that dropped the hook or put it on the wrong flag passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- That `Disable video autoplay` contract now covers the calls an Instagram post, a trend preview and an ad card make to PostVideo as well. It reads which bit of PostVideo's default mask stands for the play flag. Where a call sets that bit (the trend preview and the ad card on 450), PostVideo ignores the flag it's handed, so the hook has to clear the bit and load the default into the flag before it asks, and nothing may read either register after the call. The full-screen viewer has to stay as Threads wrote it. The register check gains test builds that skip the Instagram post, ask without clearing the bit, load the wrong default, change the viewer or read the mask again after the call, and only this contract refuses each one.
- The final APK check now holds `Pure black dark mode` to its own contract as well. It finds Threads' theme in the stock build by the note Compose leaves in it, along with the helpers the theme builds its colors in (on 450 the #101010 gray is loaded in one of those, not in the theme), and it finds the dark and light color schemes the theme reads by their colors. Every #101010 load there has to hand the gray to the extension right after, on its own register, and each of the dark scheme's #101010 backgrounds (two on 450) has to ask right before the scheme is built. The light scheme keeps its own #101010 untouched, so light mode looks as it always has. Left out, nothing may ask and those methods stay stock. Before, a build that dropped a load hook or the dark scheme's background hooks passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now holds the HushThreads row in Threads' own settings to a contract too. It finds Threads' settings list, its settings row and the row it draws Accounts Center with in the stock build by the notes Compose leaves in them, and it reads which case of the list draws More settings from the entry names Threads keeps. The patched build has to ask the extension for the HushThreads row once, right where that case ends, on the composer the case draws with. The extension's row has to call Threads' Accounts Center row with its own title, subtitle, icon and click, and the click has to be a kind Threads' row can take. Every other patch depends on `HushThreads settings`, so the check expects the row in any build with a patch selected. Before, a build that dropped the row or drew it in the wrong place passed this check, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now proves the spare registers `Sanitize sharing links` borrows are really free. Each of its link hooks puts the post's code and its author's name in registers of its own, and the hooks in Copy link and the resumed shares load the post into one as well. The check walks the stock method from the spot each hook goes in, down every branch and into the catch blocks around it, and refuses a build whose hook writes a register Threads still reads there. Before, it only checked that those registers didn't clash with each other, so a hook that wiped out a value Threads still needed passed, and only the fixture tests would've caught it.
- The final APK check now makes sure `Restore screens on re-signed builds` only borrows registers that are really spare. The patch writes three registers at the top of Threads' signature wrapper before the stock code runs, and the check requires all three to be locals of that method, below the register `this` sits in. Before, a build whose wrapper had fewer registers than the patch assumes could have the patch overwrite `this`, and it passed because the check only compared the register numbers to the ones the patch expects. Only the fixture tests would've caught it.

## Threads

- New Trust user-added certificates patch, not selected by default. Threads accepts certificates you've installed on your phone yourself, such as one a work network needs or a debugging proxy's, wherever it relies on Android's own certificate checks. Threads' network code checks Meta's certificates on its own as well and this patch doesn't change that, so a proxy still can't read most of Threads' traffic to Meta. HushThreads settings list it under Set when you patched.
- New Remove share targets patch, not selected by default. Threads stops showing up in the share sheet other apps open, so it isn't offered when you share a link, a photo or a video from somewhere else. The patch takes Threads' share entries out of its manifest, and any direct share contacts Threads might list there go too. Sharing from Threads to other apps still works. HushThreads settings list it under Set when you patched.
- New Change version code patch, not selected by default. It raises the patched Threads' version code to the highest Android allows, so Google Play stops offering Meta's updates over it. Every build with the patch has that same code, so an older Threads patched with it installs over a newer one too. Threads' own checks of its version code, at start and in its job scheduler, still see the code Meta built. Going back to stock Threads afterwards means uninstalling first, which deletes Threads' data, and later HushThreads builds need the patch too.
- Hide ads now also takes out the feed units Threads itself marks as ads by their unit type, even when the post inside doesn't carry the ad flag. That covers plain ads, ads for ads, the two kinds of ad pivot and the ads feedback prompts. Suggested accounts and other recommendation units stay, and so do ordinary posts. The Hide ads switch covers both checks.
- New Max image quality patch, off by default in Manager. Threads gets every photo in several sizes and normally loads the one closest to your screen's width. With this on it loads the largest size it has, so photos look sharper and each one is a bigger download. Square crops stay square and nothing changes size on screen. The switch is under Feed in HushThreads settings as Full size photos, and turning it off or pausing HushThreads gives Threads its own choice back.
- New Disable screenshot detection patch, off by default in Manager. Threads isn't told when you take a screenshot. It stops looking through your photos for new screenshots, and on Android 14 and newer it doesn't ask Android to report screenshots of the feed. Your screenshots are still saved. The switch sits in HushThreads' Privacy settings, and turning it off or pausing HushThreads gives Threads its own behavior back.
- Restore screens on re-signed builds now also covers FBNS, the push service Meta's apps share. FBNS checks the app's own signing certificate before it hands it pushes, and on a re-signed build it now gets Threads' original certificate there too, the same way Threads' other security checks already did. Refs #6.
- New Save photos and videos patch, selected by default. A post's menu gets a Save row right under Copy link, with Threads' own download icon. It reads Save photo, Save video or Save all, depending on what the post holds, and posts without a photo or video don't get it. A tap saves to your gallery, photos to Pictures/Threads and videos to Movies/Threads with their sound, at the best size Threads has. A carousel saves every page in order, photos and videos alike, and its files carry the post's id so two posts never mix. The menu closes once the save starts, as it does after Copy link. A new Downloads page in HushThreads settings has the switch plus quality, folder and file name options, and it shows how the last carousel save went. Pause takes the row away too.
- HushThreads now has its own row in Threads' settings, right above More settings, so you can open it from your profile's settings like any other page. It's drawn the way Threads draws its own rows. It grows with large text, and TalkBack reads it out and opens it with a double tap. The launcher shortcut and Additional settings on the App info page still work.
- HushThreads now patches Threads 450.0.0.51.78 (version code 512008342, the 240-480dpi build) as well as 449 and 448. Threads 450 rearranged the code behind three patches. Disable video autoplay now finds the flag PostVideo plays by from the check that sets the player going, Block background-return feed refresh follows the warm-start check's new branch and the second server setting 450 can read its time limit from, and Pure black dark mode also looks in the helper where 450 builds its dark colors.
- If Threads draws its settings before HushThreads has started, the HushThreads row is left out of that one draw and comes back on the next, instead of staying hidden until Threads restarts.
- On a Threads build whose settings screen has changed so the HushThreads row can't go in, the settings patch now leaves the row out and says why in the patch log, instead of failing and taking every other patch with it. HushThreads still opens from its launcher shortcut and App info.

## Tooling

- A fixture test decodes the network security config of 450, 449 and 448 and checks that the user entry lands in its base trust anchors and nothing else in the file changes.
- A fixture test decodes the manifest of 450, 449 and 448 and checks that the share handler's two share filters are the only thing that goes, and that the entry Threads uses to share out to other apps stays.
- A fixture test checks on 450, 449 and 448 that Threads' own reads of its version code go through HushThreads with their own registers, that the start-up and job scheduler checks are among them, that the two reads meant to see the raised code are left alone, and that the decoded manifest changes in its version code and nowhere else.
- A fixture test checks on 450, 449 and 448 that the unit type is read from the feed item's own field, the one its feedItemType getter reads, and that the field's enum names every ad kind. A unit test drops the ad unit types and keeps NETEGO and SUGGESTED units and ordinary posts.
- A fixture test checks on 450, 449 and 448 that Threads' one photo size chooser asks the extension for its target width first thing, and that the answer lands in the register the chooser reads that width from. The patch refuses when the chooser isn't there exactly once or reads the width anywhere else.
- A fixture test checks on 450, 449 and 448 that the photo library observer and the screenshot folder report each ask the extension before anything else, with the register they borrow unused at that point, and that Threads' one request to Android goes through the extension with the same arguments.
- A fixture test checks on 450, 449 and 448 that FBNS's check hashes the certificate HushThreads answers, read straight after its own read with nothing else moved, and that a check read twice or into the wrong register stops the patch.
- The save engine and its tests come from HushGram, with per-file provenance. A fixture test checks on 450, 449 and 448 that the Save row goes in only on Copy link's own path and is drawn with the calls Copy link uses. Every other branch in the menu still lands where it did, including 450's, where another row shares Copy link's drawing call. It refuses to patch when Copy link is checked twice, a branch jumps into its case, the menu's composer or own parameters get overwritten, or the menu closes some other way. Apart from the release check, the downloader is the only code that opens its own connection, and the hosts test now holds both to that.
- A fixture test checks on 449 and 448 that the row goes in only where Threads draws More settings, hands Threads its own composer and modifier, and refuses to patch when that entry moves, its composer gets overwritten or a branch jumps into it.
- The fixture tests run on 450, 449 and 448. On 450 they check the playback effect's new parameters, the warm-start check that jumps to its log and back, the time limit read from either of two keys and the dark colors built in a helper.
- Disable video autoplay now also checks that the flag it finds turns a video on when true and off when false, so a Threads build wired the other way round is refused instead of getting a switch that works backwards.
